name: Scaption
summary: Raise a straight arm to shoulder height about 30° in front of the side, thumb up.
setup: Face the phone with a light weight, thumb pointing up. Raise the arm in the plane of the shoulder blade — a little in front of straight out to the side — to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
brief: Stand with a light weight, thumb pointing up. Raise the arm in the plane of the shoulder blade to shoulder height, then lower slowly.
why: The upper arm rises in the camera plane, so its angle counts the reps; the shoulder hiking is the fault to watch and shows as the ear–shoulder gap closing.

show.ask: the working arm out at shoulder height, halfway between straight ahead and straight out to the side

progression: Heavier weight; both arms at once.
contraindications: Pain in the painful arc (60–120°) that does not settle.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Arm drifting straight out or forward
faults.tip: Scaption is the 30–45° plane. Straight out to the side is a different, tighter exercise.

faults.label: Thumb pointing down
faults.tip: Thumb down closes the space at the top of the shoulder. Lead with the thumb up.

faults.label: Going above shoulder height
faults.tip: The cuff works best up to horizontal; higher just adds strain.

faults.label: Dropping the arm
faults.tip: Lowering slowly is where a cuff tendon is loaded most usefully.

guide.cannotSee: Whether the arm is truly in the shoulder-blade plane.

points.t: Straight, thumb up, 30° forward of the side, to shoulder height.
Stays down and back; no hiking.
